Lesson: for self-contained batch-research tasks, prefer fresh agents over forks to avoid conversation-history contamination; always verify the output file exists on disk before trusting a batch's self-reported summary.

incident_log.resolution: Audited both on resume: retry-a HAD written a complete, valid 10-company output file just before termination (confirmed by JSON-parsing it and checking all 10 expected internal_row_ids were present) - salvaged and merged, no rework needed. wave2 batch3 produced NO output file (its self-reported 'all 10 researched, compiling now' text could not be verified against any saved data) - treated as a total loss for that batch and must be redone from scratch. process_rules_now_in_effect: Batch size: 10 companies max per research agent.
Concurrency: only ONE background research agent running at a time (reduced from 4 in parallel, to avoid another simultaneous session-limit failure across multiple agents).

Dispatch fresh general-purpose agents for these self-contained batch tasks, not forks (forks are for tasks that genuinely need this conversation's context; these don't, and forks risk context contamination as seen above).

Per-company hard cap: max 3 tool calls; no more than one retry on any single fetch/search; if identity/website/careers/LinkedIn can't be confirmed within budget, classify ambiguous_identity_manual_review (or unverifiable_identity if there is active contrary evidence) and move on - never stall.

Update this file after every single completed+merged batch, not just at wave boundaries.
